instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Rinse the 1 cup pumpkin seeds in a colander, rubbing off any pulp. Pat them dry.
Bring 1 1/4 cups water and 1/4 tsp of the salt to a boil in a small pot. Add the seeds and simmer for 5 minutes.
Drain the seeds. Spread them on a clean towel or paper towels and dry them well.
Transfer the seeds to a bowl and toss with the olive oil, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, the garlic powder, the paprika and the onion powder.
Spread the seeds in a single layer on the baking sheet.
Roast for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring once or twice, until they're golden and crunchy. Take them out before they turn dark brown.
Let them cool completely on the pan. They'll crisp up as they cool. Store them in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
method_notes: No version has a rating with 20 or more votes, so the lead is Baked Bree, which has no ratings yet but gives full amounts and a clear method. Baked Bree and Whole Foods both boil the seeds first (5 and 10 minutes) and the NC State Extension version skips the boil; all roast with oil and a simple seasoning. This follows Baked Bree's 350°F oven and 5 minute simmer, scaled down from 1 2/3 cups of seeds to 1 cup, and keeps the seasoning mild.
